title: Gilbert Bayard (Toledo) to Anne de Montmorency, 5 Jan 1526 (BnF Clairambault 325 f. 84; DECODE R2285)

documents.shelfmark: BnF Clairambault 325 f. 84 (17th-c. copy); DECODE R2285

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the copy; Champollion-Figeac 1847 prints the letter without the cipher passage.

transcription.source: DECODE R2285 images IMG_R2285_I16203/I16204 (BnF Clairambault 325 f. 84r-v)
transcription.notes: Graphic signs imitated by a 17th-c. copyist; three lines on f. 84r.

system.summary: Graphic-sign cipher, 56 signs of 29 kinds in a 17th-c. copy; same sign pool as the Raince and Calvimont alphabets of 1525-26, values unknown.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo lists it unsolved; Champollion-Figeac 1847 prints the letter omitting the cipher

conditions.human_role: Selected the target; the DECODE session cookie was supplied earlier.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R2285 images with the saved cookie; located the three cipher lines on f. 84r.
Transcribed 56 signs (29 kinds) into labels, ct.txt.
Tomokiyo cryptiana francis page: unsolved; hidden alignment with marginal note does not fit.
Champollion-Figeac 1847 no. CCXVIII prints the letter from a Brequigny copy and omits the cipher.
Biermann Calvimont key (Clair. 325 f. 67) mapped by sign shape, pinned anneal: no sense.
Raince 1526 key (Tomokiyo) with nulls ny/K removed: -3.5/sign, gibberish.
Homophonic anneal, free and constrained, 24+30 restarts: best restarts disagree; underdetermined.
BnF archives search for Gilbert Bayard originals: fr. 3005/3010/3046 (Malines 1530), fr. 2968, fr. 3921; no Toledo 1526 original, no other cipher letter.

outcome.method_basis: The three cipher lines (56 signs) on the Clairambault 325 f. 84r copy have no decipherment in the volume or in Champollion-Figeac 1847, which prints the letter without them; the Calvimont and Raince 1526 keys did not fit and ciphertext-only annealing was underdetermined.
outcome.notes: Blocked on key material and length; the original letter (V. 41 f. 4) might carry cleaner signs or a decipherment.
